text:
IncidentBot: ALERT: elevated 5xx & gateway timeouts detected for service=runtime-model-runner (route: POST /v1/generate). 5m error rate ~22%. Paging oncall: Anya

Anya: ack. i'm looking. metrics show spike in 504s at the edge + 500s from model-runner pods. starting with logs and recent deploys. any customer reports @Omar?

Omar: two 504s reported by a production customer (cust-prod-129) and one 500 from a different tenant. CS opened ticket CUST-129-504. will gather request ids.

Mike: infra note: autoscaler scaled down to 2 replicas ~10m ago due to low cpu signals; min_replicas was 2. we have OOMKilled in the pod logs and multiple SIGSEGV entries in dmesg. node metrics show burst of >1.2GB ephemeral allocation per pod.

Jess: that sounds like a recent matmul kernel change in the quantized path. I see a commit landed earlier today that touches matmul_fuse. tagging @runtime. If kernel corrupts large buffers, it will cause segfaults under long sequence lengths.

Anya: collecting pod logs now:

```
kubectl -n runtime logs runtime-model-runner-7f4c8 -c runner --since=20m
# shows repeated: "terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'" then "segfault at ... ip ..."
```

Anya: also seeing gateway timeouts at the edge due to slow retries. we should stop retrying to avoid amplification. Mike can we disable external retry policy for this route?

Mike: doing that now. patching envoy retries:

```
envoyctl set-route /v1/generate --retries 0 --apply
```

Mike: done. also bumping min_replicas to 4 to avoid bad downscaling during noisy allocs.

Jess: idea for immediate mitigation: rollback the matmul kernel to previous stable build (image rdm-runtime:20260227-stable) or apply a quick guard to bounds-check allocations. rollback is faster. can we do a rollback to the previous image in the affected pool?

DeployBot: rollback requested by Jess. initiating rollback for runtime-model-runner to image rdm-runtime:20260227-stable on pool runtime-pool-1.

Anya: initiating traffic steering: route 60% to fallback pool (runtime-pool-fallback-small) that uses a different model variant with smaller memory footprint; keep 40% to original for debug traces.

DeployBot: traffic split updated.

(5m later)

Anya: 5xx dropped from 22% -> 7%. still seeing occasional SIGSEGVs on a subset of pods that haven't been drained. Mike can you cordon the nodes with recent crashes?

Mike: cordoning nodes gnode-21 and gnode-22 and draining pods.

```
kubectl cordon gnode-21
kubectl drain gnode-21 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```

Mike: nodes cordoned and pods rescheduled. new pods come up with stable memory usage.

Jess: rollback finished on 3/4 replicas; canary pods show no segfaults in last 6m. i'm preparing a hotfix PR with additional bounds checks and an internal allocation guard (will add telemetry for large matmul allocations). estimate 45m for full CI + rollout.

Anya: good. customer comms: Omar please send an initial incident ack to affected customers and note mitigation steps.

Omar: ack. message posted to CUST-129-504 and CUST-231-500. offering status updates and ETA for full fix.

Product Ops: noted. tagging as severity S2. capturing SLA exposure and impacted tenants.

(25m later)

Jess: hotfix PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/499. includes: fallback checks in quantized_matmul.cc, allocation telemetry, and a defensive early-return for sequences > 4096 tokens. unit + integration tests added; CI green for linux-x86.

DeployBot: starting canary rollout of rdm-runtime:hotfix-20260228-1 to runtime-pool-1 with 2 pods. health checks enabled.

Anya: monitoring canary and metrics. current cluster 5xx ~0.9%, gateway timeouts down.

Mike: removing retry disable once we confirm stability. plan: keep retry=0 for 30m after full rollout.

Anya: handoff note to night oncall @Sam coming up in 30m: current status: traffic split 60/40 to fallback, rollback performed, hotfix canary passing, 5xx ~0.7%. ongoing tasks: monitor canary, watch for segfaults/core drops, if recurring then escalate to infra for potential hardware issues.

Sam: ack — i'll take over. please post runbook link and confirm when routing reverts.

Anya: runbook added: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/runtime-matmul-segfault. Routing auto-revert scheduled in 1h30m unless extended.

(1h later)

Sam: canary promoted to prod, full rollout completed. 5xx stabilized at ~0.15%. no new OOMs. routing reverted back to previous single pool.

Omar: closed immediate customer tickets with post-fix notification. customers asked to reopen if they see further issues.

Product Ops: incident recorded for postmortem. Please include timeline, root cause (regression in quantized matmul kernel causing allocation corruption under long sequences), mitigations (rollback, increased min_replicas, node drains, hotfix), and action items: add allocation telemetry, add sequence-length caps, strengthen pre-merge perf tests for quantized paths.

IncidentBot: Incident resolved. Start: 1767198765. End: 1767200501. Severity: S2. Follow-ups assigned: runtime PR merge & rollout, telemetry dashboard, update runbook.

Anya: thanks everyone. great cross-team response. i'll draft the postmortem and link PRs/runs in the doc. Sam, will you lead next steps on telemetry?

Sam: sure, I'll coordinate with Jess and Mike.
